title: Baking bread with Priya
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). Alex and Priya bake sourdough, covering the starter, hydration and kneading versus stretch and folds, contrast baking with cooking risotto, link bread to carb timing for long runs, and Alex's promise to send the brother's sourdough photos is never picked up.

utterances.text: Okay, what is that jar? It looks alive.
It is alive. That's my sourdough starter. Flour and water, plus wild yeast that moved in on its own.
That's slightly horrifying. Does it have a name?
Not yet. My brother named his Loafy McLoafface, so the bar is low.
Ha. Okay, how is this different from risotto night? You were very bossy about stirring.
Totally different. With risotto you're right there the whole time, tasting and adjusting. You fix it as you go.
And bread?
You can't taste bread until the end. You weigh everything, mix it, and then wait for hours. Baking is chemistry. Risotto is more like jazz.
Okay, so why are we weighing things?
Hydration. It's how much water compared to flour. This one's seventy-five percent, so seven hundred fifty grams of water per kilo of flour.
Is that a lot?
It's pretty wet. Higher hydration gives you those big holes inside, but it's sticky and harder to shape.
It's definitely sticky. It's all over my hands.
Wet your hands first. Now, normally you'd knead it, but with dough this wet we do stretch and folds instead.
What's the difference?
Kneading is ten minutes of pushing it around the counter. Stretch and fold is, every half hour, grab one side, stretch it up, fold it over, turn the bowl, four times. Then leave it alone.
So less work, more waiting.
Exactly. The gluten builds by itself while it rests. Kneading just does it faster with muscle.
Wait, that's your running thing. Rest days are training.
Ha, Jordan would love that. Actually, this bread is partly for running.
Of course it is.
Jordan says to eat carbs a couple of hours before a long run, not right before, and something easy to digest. So toast with honey at seven for a nine o'clock run.
And after?
Protein and more carbs, like eggs on toast. Timing matters more than I thought.
Okay. Can I come back for the first slice?
Obviously, it bakes tomorrow morning. Oh, and remind me to send you my brother's sourdough photos later. His loaves are absurdly pretty.
Sure. Okay, fold number three?
Fold number three. Grab, stretch, fold, turn.
This is weirdly calming. Like stirring risotto, but with more waiting.
